title: SwiftVLM: Efficient Vision-Language Model Inference via Cross-Layer Token Bypass
claim: Prior pruning discards or merges tokens irreversibly in shallow layers; ours bypasses them forward so deeper layers can reconsider them.
layout: 3 panels: two top (a, b), one wide bottom (c); green bypass arc
description: Three panels compare visual token reduction across layers. Panels (a) Merge and (b) Drop sit side by side at the top, separated by a dashed divider. Each shows vertical Layer boxes (i, i+1, ..., k-1, k) holding small cream token squares. In (a), blue arrows merge several tokens into one hatched token. In (b), dark grey tokens are dropped, and dotted grey arrows carry the surviving tokens forward. Panel (c) Bypass spans the bottom and uses the same layer sequence, starting with a stack of input vision tokens. A green arc labeled Bypass runs from layer i to a dashed box labeled Token Alignment before layer k. Inside the box, the merged token is restored into the original tokens. The green highlights make the proposed method stand out from the blue and grey prior approaches.
caption: Comparison of visual token pruning strategies in VLMs. (a)–(b) Existing approaches suffer from irreversible loss of critical visual information once tokens are merged or dropped in shallow layers. (c) We propose Bypass, a pruning strategy that restores previously merged tokens via token alignment. Bypass provides critical visual tokens with an opportunity to be reconsidered at deeper layers with stronger token selection capability.
abstract: Visual token pruning is a promising approach for reducing the computational cost of vision-language models (VLMs), and existing methods often rely on early pruning decisions to improve efficiency. While effective on coarse-grained reasoning tasks, they suffer from significant performance degradation on tasks requiring fine-grained visual details. Through layer-wise analysis, we reveal substantial discrepancies in visual token importance across layers, showing that tokens deemed unimportant at shallow layers can later become highly relevant for text-conditioned reasoning. To avoid irreversible critical information loss caused by premature pruning, we introduce a new pruning paradigm, termed bypass, which preserves unselected visual tokens and forwards them to subsequent pruning stages for re-evaluation. Building on this paradigm, we propose SwiftVLM, a simple and training-free method that performs pruning at model-specific layers with strong visual token selection capability, while enabling independent pruning decisions across layers. Experiments across multiple VLMs and benchmarks demonstrate that SwiftVLM consistently outperforms existing pruning strategies, achieving superior accuracy-efficiency trade-offs and more faithful visual token selection behavior.
